Studio now tells a call from the request it sent, says why a request got no answer and why a stream cannot connect, and keeps the credentials in error texts off everything that leaves its page. Its Playground reaches a proxy that admits browsers only, and the app's own address is learned from its server, never from a request. Nothing in your code changes — update every `@noverax` package together.

### Update every package together

- **Install 0.3.1 of every `@noverax` package at once.** An adapter from 0.3.0 beside a 0.3.1 core still tells the app's origin as its request's `Host` named it: only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` are taken from it, with one warning to update. A 0.3.1 runtime tells Studio how each stream's connection stands, which an older Studio does not know, and notes in its log as a rejected event.

### Security

- **The app's origin is learned from its server, never from a request.** Studio's Playground sends a Proxy-mode call — its headers and the `Authorization` you typed among them — to the app's own origin. In 0.3.0 that origin was learned from the first request's `Host`, so a request with a chosen `Host`, or a page whose name pointed at your machine, could send those calls to another host. Each adapter now tells the address its server listens on: the socket a request arrived on, the address `next dev` records as it starts, the one Studio's Vite plugin or Nuxt module sees the dev server listen on. Express, Fastify, NestJS, Hono and SolidStart learn it from the first request a Courier route serves; Next.js, SvelteKit, Astro, React Router and Nuxt before any request. See [How the app learns its origin](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/api/config#app-origin).
- **A stream the proxy relays keeps to its upstream's origin.** Its upstream connection followed any redirect with the source's headers, and handed another host's events on to the page. It now follows a redirect only on the upstream's own origin, as a proxied call does; a redirect elsewhere refuses the stream with `4000` plus the status, and a source that names its own `redirect` keeps it.
- **A Playground call keeps to the route's origin.** It followed any redirect the route, or a middleware in front of it, answered with, and took its headers along. It now follows a redirect only on the route's own origin, and says why it stopped at one it did not follow: the route's own, or the API's, which the proxy answers with its status alone.
- **Error texts lose their credentials as they leave Studio's page.** Studio wrote a failure's text as the app was told it — into `.courier/studio.db`, saved sessions and their exports, and what an agent is told. The page opened from Studio's link still shows each text whole; everything that leaves it has the credentials in its texts cut: an address's user, password and secret parameters, a header value the platform quoted, a JWT or a provider's key, a credential after `Bearer` or `Basic`, the value of a pair named as a secret. Your app cuts nothing and ships no code for it. See [Studio](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/overview#start-studio).
- **`@noverax/courier-server` lets only the pages `allowedOrigins` lists read its answers.** It let a page whose origin read as the server's own read them too, with the user's cookies. The server's own page never needs that; behind a proxy that ends TLS and is not trusted with its forwarded scheme, the server reads its own address as `http:`, so a page on that plain-HTTP origin, in a browser that sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site`, could read what its HTTPS users were answered. Each answer past its health check, a refusal too, now varies by `Origin`, so a cache in between keeps them apart.
- **A specification fetch without the token reaches no host through a fake-IP proxy.** A fake-IP proxy — Clash, Surge, sing-box — answers every name with an address of 198.18.0.0/15 and takes it to the host the name was, a host of your network among them, and Studio took that range for the public internet: a page or process without the project's token, such as a machine on the network Studio was bound to with `--host 0.0.0.0`, could reach such a host through it. It is now refused. With the token a name still goes through the proxy, and such an address written out in a URL or a redirect is reached only when `studio.allowedSpecHosts` names it. See [Import an API](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/import-api).
- **Studio writes a specification's values into code only when they can be nothing else.** A specification sent back to Studio to generate, write, update or add endpoints from had some of its values written into the code as they came: a schema's name, a name a schema refers to by, a group's, a schema's type, a bound, a pattern, an encoding's `explode`. Studio's parser gives each of them safe, so an imported specification never could, but one crafted and sent with the project's token became code in the project. Before a line is generated, each is now held to a kind that can only be what it says — a name of identifier characters that no generated file keeps for itself, a type a schema has, a finite number, a flag, a pattern whose literal ends where it does — and every name the client is called by to one it can be called by; anything else is refused with `400`, naming where it is — with `INVALID_SPEC` when Studio writes, updates or adds endpoints from it, and as the transform's `IMPORT_TRANSFORM_FAILED` when an import's `transform` returns it. Adding endpoints from a specification the generator cannot follow answers `400`, as writing does, where it answered `500`.
- **A source's name stays a name in the routes module.** `courier.routes.ts` names each source in a comment above its routes, and wrote the name as it stood: one holding `*/` — a name Studio was sent to import an API under with the project's token, or one `courier.config.ts` declares — ended the comment, and the rest of the name became code in a module every page using the proxy client loads. The name's `*/` is now broken, as Studio's generator breaks one in a description.
- **A project file is checked by its name before the disk is asked about it.** The checks Studio's file work goes through — an import's writes, a specification read from the project, a recorded test — followed links and compared where they led, and trusted their caller to have kept the path inside the project first. Each now refuses a path outside the project by its name before it looks the path up, so one that skipped that step reads, lists or writes nothing.
- **Studio's code generator escapes what would end a script.** Every value a specification gives that the generator writes as a string — a path, a base URL, a media type, the name of a query parameter, a form field or a header, a description, an enum member — is written with `<`, `>` and the two line separators escaped, so a generated string stays whole wherever the code is put, and an update or a move of an endpoint keeps it escaped. A description written into a comment has its `</script` and `<!--` broken too; a pattern is written as the specification gives it. Code generated again from a specification with HTML in its descriptions changes once.

### Defining APIs

- **An ArkType schema with a `Date` or a check of its own is described.** ArkType writes no JSON Schema for a `Date`, a `.narrow()` or another part JSON has no form for, and refused the whole schema, so `toOpenAPI`, an agent's tools and Studio's [Contract Drift](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/contract-drift) left such a schema unspecified. Only that part is now left unspecified, as with Zod, and the rest of the schema is written.

### Studio

- **A call is told apart from the request it sent.** Two identical reads made together send one request, and the second call waits for the first's answer. Studio's network figures — latency, throughput, bytes and error rates, the Audit's findings on size and caching, a session's figures, its HAR and Postman exports — now count requests; the Timeline's rows, the Middleware page and an agent's list count every call, and where the two differ both are shown: `14 calls · 5 requests`. A call another call's request answered is marked `shared`, its Timing tab says whose request it waited for, and a failed or slow request is toasted once, however many calls it answered. The request belongs to the first call still waiting when its answer comes: a call that left is never shared. See [Audit](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/audit).
- **A request that got no answer says why.** Its Error tab names the system's code — `ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`, a certificate's, Bun's own — once, with the platform's text under the message; its Response tab, and the Playground's, say there was no answer instead of an empty body; and the suggested fix follows the code: a host name that did not resolve, a connection that failed, a certificate not trusted, an answer that broke as it arrived, an API that sent no headers in time, redirects with no end. A request a middleware failed because a connection of its own was refused says why too.
- **The Playground starts each endpoint with variables its schema takes.** An optional enum started as an empty string, which its schema refused, so the first send of an endpoint with one failed with `422`; so did a literal, a union, a string format, a nested object, and every optional Valibot field. Each field now starts as a value of its own kind within its bounds — an enum's first value, a known format's sample, a nested object filled in — and one whose check Studio cannot read is left out when it may be. A numeric TypeScript enum is listed by its numbers, not the names it maps them back to.
- **A call the input schema refused says it was not sent.** Its Response tab, and the Playground's, said the server had answered with an empty body — also of a call refused in Direct mode, with no server asked — its status read *schema mismatch*, the line under the variables said they were valid, and a toast said a request had failed. They now say the call was not sent and what the schema said of the first field it refused; the status reads *variables refused*, the line under the variables keeps the refusal until they change, and the toast says the input schema refused it.
- **A stream that cannot connect says so.** It stood open and live while its client reconnected without a word. Its Messages tab and its Overview now say it is reconnecting, why its last connection ended, how many connections in a row failed and when the next one opens; the lists say *retrying*, and one that gives up before any connection opened says so, with the code and the fix. A stream the proxy relays tells how its upstream connection stands, and an ended stream says who closed it — its server, its caller, its lifetime, a server that shut down — where Studio said the server had completed every one.
- **The Playground reaches a proxy with `browsersOnly`.** A Proxy-mode call runs from your server's process, which sends no browser's headers, so `browsersOnly` refused every one with `403`. In development Studio's runtime now gives each call a one-time pass the proxy redeems: only `browsersOnly` is passed over, every other check applies, and no pass is honoured in production. Where the route cannot redeem it — an Edge route, a worker, a remote `appOrigin`, a runtime whose request headers cannot change — the Playground says why and offers to run the call in Direct mode. See [Proxy Mode](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/proxy-mode/overview).
- **A tag or an import named `eval`, `arguments`, `undefined` or `globalThis` makes code that works.** Each was bound under its own name. A module, strict as every module is, cannot bind `eval` or `arguments`, so the import's code did not load; a binding named `undefined` or `globalThis` took the place of the value the generated code reads by that name — the `undefined` a call passes for a body it does not send, the `globalThis` a secret is read from — and so did a query parameter of such a name, whose value was then sent as the body. A tag such as `Global This` named its group `globalThis`. Such a group or import is now named as a reserved word's is, `evalGroup` in `eval-group/`, and such a parameter is taken under a local name of its own. An update, Manage and a write refuse an import 0.3.0 wrote under such a name with `IMPORT_RENAMED`, where they wrote a second copy beside the one the config imports or found none of its endpoints: remove it, which takes its files from the folder 0.3.0 wrote, then import it again. A group 0.3.0 named so takes its new name the next time the import is written, and Manage keeps its endpoints.
- **A parameter or a field named like a member every object has is one like any other.** A query parameter named `constructor` or `__proto__` that the caller left out was sent all the same, as `function Object() { [native code] }` or as the variables' prototype; it is now sent only when given. An optional field named `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf` or another member TypeScript reads on every object made its type take no object that left the field out, so a call without it did not compile; it is now typed with that member beside its own type. A name `__proto__` is written as a key of its own wherever the generated code builds an object, where it set the object's prototype, and an endpoint may not be named so. The runtime keeps such a name too: `formQuery`'s values, the variables left beside `headerVariablesMiddleware`'s headers, a path parameter, a variable's default — one named `constructor` was never filled in — the headers a call merges and those a Node answer is written with, and the body Studio is shown.
- **A parameter named like one of the language's globals passes the linter.** A query parameter named `Date`, `String` or `constructor` beside a body was bound in the generated call under its own name, which hid the global from the code beside it, and Biome's recommended rules refused the file. It is now taken under a local name of its own, and sent as before.
- **A generated call that sends no body writes `void 0`.** It wrote `undefined`, which a binding of that name in the same file — the import 0.3.0 wrote for a group named `undefined` — took the place of, and which kept that import counted as used after an update renamed the group. A generated file changes there once.
- **An import that selects a nested tag keeps the tag it sits in.** Its `include` and `exclude` dropped an OpenAPI 3.2 parent tag left with no endpoint of its own, so the tags inside it were generated in no group and their endpoints could not be called. The parent is now kept while a tag inside it keeps an endpoint.
- **An update that drops a group removes its file.** An update that dropped a group from an API whose `source.ts` also holds endpoints of its own kept `source.ts` importing the group's file, so the file stayed, though the update said it was removed. The import now goes with the group, unless code you kept in `source.ts` uses it.
- **The preview of a write, an update or Manage shows the files the apply keeps.** A file the plan would remove that another file staying imports is kept when the plan is applied, so the project still compiles; the preview listed it as removed. It now lists it as kept, as the apply does.
- **Groups whose names clash in one file are imported under names of their own.** An OpenAPI 3.2 tag `pets group` around a tag `pets` made the parent's file import `pets as petsGroup` beside its own `petsGroup`, which does not compile. A group is now imported under a name its file binds to nothing else — `petsGroup_2` there — and so is one a transform names like the source's alias or a schema's constant. **Manage** does the same where it adds a group, and no longer lists one under a name the file binds to something else. Two groups written to one folder, as `con` and `_con`, are refused with `INVALID_SPEC` rather than one overwriting the other.
- **A source a page calls by a relative address can be declared from its traffic.** A page whose source has a relative base URL records each call by its path, `/api/pets`, and reading a document from such calls threw for the whole batch, or, through Studio, left each one out as a call with no answer. A path is now read against the origin of the page that made it, which the page sends with its calls; with no origin known, the document's server is the path alone. A call with no address Studio can read is counted apart, and the wizard names it so.
- **A specification with a malformed escape in a reference is read.** One `$ref` such as `#/components/schemas/%zz` failed the whole read with *URI malformed*. It now points nowhere, as a reference to a part the document lacks does: the schema it names is typed as unknown, a parameter or a path item it names is left out, and each is said so.
- **A reference to a part the specification does not hold is said so, and typed as unknown.** A reference to a component nobody declares named that component in the generated code, as a type and a schema nothing declared, so the code did not compile. Such a reference, one into another file, and one through an escape that decodes to no text are now read as unknown — an operation whose body points nowhere as one without a body — and the import lists each place the specification writes one among what it left out, by its JSON pointer: the wizard counts them as missing references, and `courier-studio import` prints them.
- **A path parameter is filled whatever its name.** A path parameter named with a dot or a leading digit — `{id.v}`, `{1st}` — was left in the path as written, so each call sent the braces instead of the value. It is now named as a placeholder can read it, `:id_v`, `:_1st`, alike in the path and in the variables. An operation whose path puts a parameter right before a letter, a digit or `_`, as `/items/{id}5`, made code that did not compile; no Courier path can write it, so it is left out, and the import says why.
- **A YAML schema that holds itself through an alias is read.** `Tree: &tree { properties: { child: *tree } }` put the tree inside itself, and reading it followed it down until the read failed with *Maximum call stack size exceeded*. Where an alias brings an object back inside itself, it is now read as a reference to that object, so the tree's child is typed as a tree.
- **A schema composed of itself is read.** An `allOf` that takes in the schema it sits in — a category's `parent` composed of the category and a `depth`, a node's `children` composed of the node — was merged again inside itself until the read failed with *Maximum call stack size exceeded*. Such a composition is now declared as a schema of its own, named after where the specification writes it — `CategoryParent`, `NodeChildrenItem` — and referring to itself, so every level of it is typed and checked: a parent's parent without its `depth` is refused.
- **A property composed of two schemas takes the fields of both.** A property whose `allOf` names two schemas — `allOf: [Address, GeoPoint]` — was typed as the first alone, so the second's fields were missing from its type and went unchecked. It now takes the fields of every schema it composes, as a schema composed the same way already did.
- **A reference annotated beside it in an `allOf` keeps what the annotation says.** `allOf: [{ $ref: Pet }, { description: …, nullable: true }]`, how OpenAPI 3.0 annotates a reference, lost its description and its `nullable`: the property was typed as `Pet`, never `null`, and had no doc comment. It now keeps both.
- **A schema that is only a reference to itself is read as unknown.** `Tag: { $ref: Tag }`, or two schemas that only refer to each other, made a type that referred to itself, which does not compile. Such a schema names no value at all, so every value is one: it is read as unknown, and a schema referring to it stays a reference.
- **A file that calls no validation library imports none.** A request body extended only with parameters that are named schemas — `UserSchema.extend({ q: UserSchema })` — called no zod or ArkType function, yet its file imported the library, which a project compiling with `noUnusedLocals` refused. The import now comes only with a call.
- **A specification whose tags nest deep is read at once.** OpenAPI 3.2 tags nested under one another were read again for every tag above them: a chain of 1 000 took some ten seconds, and one of 3 000 failed with *Maximum call stack size exceeded*. Each tag and each path is now read once, so 10 000 levels read in well under a second.
- **A Postman collection whose folders nest deep is read.** Folders nested some 3 000 deep failed the read with *Maximum call stack size exceeded*. They are now walked without recursion, however deep they nest, and read as before.
- **A specification of some 125 000 operations or more is grouped by path.** Grouping by path spread the length of every path into one call, which so many paths overflowed, and gathered the endpoints of a segment by copying its list for each one. It now folds the lengths and adds each endpoint to its segment's list: 300 000 endpoints group in under half a second.
- **A specification nested some 2 000 levels deep is written and updated.** Its hash, which an import records and an update compares, is the hash of its JSON text, which `JSON.stringify` could not write past some 2 000 levels: a write of it answered 500. Past that depth the same text is now written without recursion, so it is hashed, and every hash recorded before stays as it was.
- **An import's `transform` gets its copy of a specification however deep it nests.** The copy was made with `structuredClone`, whose recursion stops some 700 objects deep, short of what the parser reads: every update of such an import failed there. It is now copied through its JSON text.
- **A specification nested deeper than Node copies between processes is generated from and compared.** For a caller without the token, generating code and comparing two specifications run in a process of their own, which Node handed the specification with a recursion of its own that stops some thousands of levels deep, short of what the parser reads: such a specification was refused as more than Studio works on. It now goes as its JSON text. Where the work itself runs out of stack on a specification, it is refused as nesting its schemas deeper than Studio can read, generate code for or compare, rather than with *Maximum call stack size exceeded*.
- **A tag, a folder or a path segment over 128 characters names a group.** Generation refused a group's name over 128 characters, the longest a folder is named from, so the import failed with `INVALID_IMPORT` — and so did two tags of 128 characters, the second numbered to 129. Such a name is now cut to 128 characters, its number included.
- **A group whose tag spells no name is named after its paths.** A tag or a Postman folder with no letter or digit Studio spells in Latin letters named its group `group`, the next one `group2`, and so on, whatever its endpoints were. It is now named after the last segment every path of the group shares: `users` for `/api/users` and `/api/users/{id}`. An import generated before takes these names the next time it is written — by an update, by Manage, or imported again — and Manage keeps each renamed group's endpoints: it reads the group's old file as the group it is now, as it does a group whose number moved, `group3` named `group` now. The old file goes as a left-out group's does, at once when Studio wrote it and nobody changed it, once you allow it when you did; what you changed in it is not carried into the group's new file.
- **An import is named after a long title within 128 characters.** Import API and `courier-studio import` named an import after its specification's whole title, so a title of some 130 characters or more gave a name the write then refused with `INVALID_IMPORT`. The name now keeps the title's first words that fit in 128 characters.
- **A failure counts the same on every screen.** An answer its schema refused counts as failed on the status bar and Welcome, as it does in Analytics, the Explorer and the Audit.
- **A mock that is still starting stops at once.** Stopping it waited until its worker had run the mocks file's code — its modules, and whatever the file does as it loads — for up to five seconds. A worker that serves nothing yet is now ended at once; one that serves is still asked to stop, so the requests it is serving finish.
- **A cancelled call is no failure.** A read a component cancelled as it went away, or a newer read took the place of, no longer toasts *Request failed*.
- **Settings → Recording names its limit Max calls**, since every call is a row of its own.
- The Courier mark keeps an icon's clear room in the Copy as menu and a request's snippets.

### Streams

- **A stream a Courier server serves opens at once.** It wrote nothing before its first event or its first heartbeat 25 s in, and a client heard it open only then; it now writes a comment as it opens, which every client passes over.
- **An answer whose body breaks off is cut off, not ended.** Express, Fastify, NestJS and `@noverax/courier-server` ended an answer whose body failed part-way — a streamed call whose upstream dropped its connection — as if it were whole: its client took the part sent for the whole answer, or, when the answer stated its length, waited for the rest. The connection is now cut, so the client learns the answer broke, and the response is marked ended, so no framework answers it again — an adapter of 0.3.0 beside this core included. Express's handler run as a plain Node listener, with no `next`, logs the failure, where it threw trying to answer `500` over the answer already sent. Fastify's plugin takes the reply over before it streams an answer, so Fastify's `handlerTimeout` no longer answers `503` over a stream still running, which threw; an answer cut this way runs no `onResponse` hook, as no stream that fails on Fastify does, and the failure is logged instead.
- **A channel whose socket cannot connect retries on Node 22.** Node 22's WebSocket reports a refused connection with an error alone and leaves its socket connecting, so a channel — a relayed one too — whose server was down stood connecting for good. It is now closed and retried as on every other runtime, and Studio is told why in the platform's own words.
- **A stream refused with a redirect it does not follow ends**, with `4000` plus the status, as one refused with a 4xx does, rather than asking again on every reconnection. A 408, a 429 and a 5xx are retried as a dropped connection is. See [Realtime](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/advanced/realtime).

### Editors and agents

- **The VS Code extension's hints show the requests beside the calls**, where reads another call's request answered sent none, and the streams reconnecting apart from the ones open.
- **An agent is told calls and requests apart**, and every error text it reads with its credentials cut.

### create-courier

- **A project set up already is offered only what it lacks**, with what holds there said and nothing more; a part counts as done only where the app loads it.
- **It reads more of a project as it is**: its path aliases, a CommonJS config, a config under any name Studio reads, the files React Router, Remix, a Cloudflare worker and Fastify's autoload start from, JSX pages that hold closing tags or prose, the modules a file loads past a comment, and every star of an import's target.
- **It changes a project with care**: `package.json` keeps its layout, a peer or optional package counts only once it is installed, no name is bound twice, routes are mounted under a name left free, React Router's routes list none twice, no config is imported from outside a `rootDir`, a Next.js config that loads Studio is given its whole function, and the `routes` script is added only where a routes module or an `.expose(` is.
- **Hono is told apart in dev dependencies**, alone or beside the mock's.

All twenty packages move to 0.3.1.

[Documentation](https://courier.noverax.cloud) · [Security policy](https://github.com/NoveraX/courier/security/policy) · [Contributing](https://github.com/NoveraX/courier/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
